passages.title: Subject: New way to claim travel costs
lines: To: All staff
From: Grace Liu, Finance Department

Starting on July 1, we will change the way travel costs are paid back. Until now, employees have filled out a paper form and waited about three weeks for their money. Under the new system, you will enter each cost in our online expense tool and add a photo of the receipt. Most requests should then be paid within five working days.

Please note a few rules. Taxi fares are paid back only when no train or bus is available, or when you travel after 10 p.m. Hotel costs are covered up to $150 a night. Meals are covered up to $40 a day, but wine is not included. Any single cost over $500 must be approved by your manager before you pay it.

The finance team will hold two short training sessions on the new tool, on June 24 and June 26, both at 3 p.m. in Room 410. Each session will last about thirty minutes. If you cannot attend either one, a simple guide will be posted on the company website by June 20.
Paper forms will still be accepted for trips taken before July 1, as long as they reach us by July 15. After that date, all requests must go through the online tool.
If you have any questions, please call me at extension 2245.

questions.en: What is the purpose of the email?
questions.zh: 這封電子郵件的目的是什麼？
options: To explain a new way of getting travel costs paid back
To announce a new limit on business trips
To invite managers to approve large costs
To remind staff that a website will be updated

questions.en: Under the new rules, which of the following will NOT be paid back?
questions.zh: 在新規定下，下列哪一項不會被報銷？
options: A $120 hotel room for one night
A taxi ride back to the hotel at 11 p.m.
A glass of wine at a dinner with a client
A $35 lunch on a business trip

questions.en: What is suggested about an employee who returned from a trip on June 28?
questions.zh: 關於一位六月二十八日出差回來的員工，文中暗示了什麼？
options: The employee must attend a session in Room 410.
The employee can still send in a paper form.
The employee will be paid within five working days.
The employee needs a manager to approve every cost.

passages.title: Now Hiring: Marketing Coordinator
lines: Our company, Norwood Lighting, makes desk and floor lamps. We are seeking a marketing coordinator for our headquarters in Taichung. This job is full time, Monday to Friday, 9 a.m. to 6 p.m.

The coordinator will plan our social media campaigns, prepare flyers for trade shows, and work closely with our design team. He or she will also manage a small budget for online ads and report the results to the marketing manager every month.

Applicants should have at least two years of experience in marketing and be fluent in both Chinese and English. Experience with survey tools is desirable but not required. Above all, we are looking for someone curious and energetic who enjoys sharing new ideas.

We offer a good salary, a yearly bonus based on performance, and fourteen days of paid leave. In their first year, new employees can also spend up to $500 on training courses, paid for by the company.

To apply, please email your résumé and a short cover letter to our HR department by Friday, May 9. Applicants who are selected will be invited to a first interview the following week. The second interview will include a short presentation on a product of your choice.

questions.en: The word "desirable" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to
questions.zh: 第三段的 "desirable" 意思最接近
options: necessary
easy to learn
popular
helpful to have

questions.en: What is NOT mentioned as a duty of the coordinator?
questions.zh: 下列哪一項沒有被列為這個職位的工作內容？
options: Planning online campaigns
Interviewing new staff
Making materials for trade shows
Reporting on the results of ads

questions.en: What will applicants who reach the second interview probably need to do?
questions.zh: 進入第二次面試的應徵者可能需要做什麼？
options: Give a talk about a product
Bring a survey they designed
Send another cover letter
Take a Chinese language test

passages.title: Notice: Our Kaohsiung office is moving
lines: From Monday, October 6, our Kaohsiung branch will move from the Harbor Building to a larger office at 88 Zhongshan Road. The new office is only a short walk from Central Park subway station and has ample parking in the basement, so it will be much easier for clients to visit us.

The move will take place over the weekend of October 4 and 5. A moving company will pack all furniture and computers on Friday afternoon, so please clear your desk and put your personal items in the boxes provided by 3 p.m. that day. Each box should be marked with your name and team. Anything left in the old office after Friday will be thrown away.

Please note that the phone lines and the internet will be unavailable from Friday at 5 p.m. until Monday at 9 a.m. If you expect an urgent call from a client during this time, give the client your mobile number in advance.

On Monday morning, the office manager, Mr. Tsai, will be at the front desk from 8:30 to give everyone a new key card. A short welcome breakfast will be served in the kitchen on the fifth floor. Thank you for your patience during the move. We hope you enjoy the new space.

questions.en: What is mentioned about the new office?
questions.zh: 文中提到新辦公室的什麼事？
options: It is in the Harbor Building.
It has a kitchen on every floor.
It is close to public transportation.
It will first open on a Saturday.

questions.en: The word "clear" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to
questions.zh: 第二段的 "clear" 意思最接近
options: explain
check
mark
empty

questions.en: What is suggested about the weekend of October 4 and 5?
questions.zh: 關於十月四日和五日那個週末，文中暗示了什麼？
options: Clients may not be able to reach the office by phone.
Employees will have to work in the new office.
Mr. Tsai will give out new key cards.
A breakfast will be served in the old office.

passages.title: Subject: Results of our customer survey
lines: To: Marketing team
From: Daniel Kao
Hi everyone,

The results of last month's online survey are in, and I want to share the main points before our meeting on Thursday. We received 1,240 responses, nearly twice as many as we expected, so thank you all for sharing the link so widely.

First, price is clearly the most important factor. About 60 percent of respondents said they would not pay more than $50 for a desk lamp. Design came second, and brand name was third. Also, people under 30 cared about design much more than older buyers did.

Second, most respondents said they learn about new products from short videos online, not from magazines. Only 8 percent had seen our magazine ads this year, even though those ads used about a third of our budget.

Based on these results, I suggest two changes for our next campaign. We should move most of the magazine budget to online videos, and we should consider a smaller, cheaper version of our desk lamp for younger buyers.
Please read the full report, which I have attached, and bring your ideas to Thursday's meeting. Ms. Ortiz from the finance team will join us to discuss the budget.
Best, Daniel

questions.en: What is indicated about the survey?
questions.zh: 文中提到這份調查的什麼事？
options: It was handed out to shoppers in stores.
More people answered it than the team had expected.
Most of the people who answered were under 30.
It will be sent out again before Thursday.

questions.en: The word "consider" in paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to
questions.zh: 第四段的 "consider" 意思最接近
options: pay for
respect
remember
think about

questions.en: What is suggested about the company's magazine ads?
questions.zh: 關於公司的雜誌廣告，文中暗示了什麼？
options: They were seen by most respondents.
They were designed for people under 30.
They cost a lot but reached few people.
They will be used again in the next campaign.

passages.title: Notice: Visitor Rules for the Assembly Floor
lines: Starting next Monday, all visitors to the Riverside factory, including staff from our head office, must follow the rules below. These rules were updated after a safety inspection last month.

Before you enter the assembly floor, please sign in at the security desk and watch a short safety video. The video takes about ten minutes. You will then receive a visitor badge, which must be worn at all times.

Every visitor must wear a hard hat and safety glasses, which are provided at the entrance. Closed shoes are required, and visitors without them will not be allowed on the floor. Please stay inside the yellow lines and do not touch any machines or parts, even if they are not running.

Photos are not permitted on the assembly floor, because some of our products have not been launched yet. If you need pictures for a report or a presentation, please ask the communications office. It can provide approved photos within two working days.
Groups of more than six people must book their visit at least three days in advance by calling extension 310. Each group will be accompanied by a member of the safety team.
Thank you for helping us keep our factory safe.

questions.en: What is NOT required of every visitor?
questions.zh: 下列哪一項不是每位訪客都必須做的？
options: Booking the visit three days in advance
Watching a safety video
Wearing a visitor badge
Wearing safety glasses

questions.en: The word "permitted" in paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to
questions.zh: 第四段的 "permitted" 意思最接近
options: printed
needed
allowed
checked

questions.en: What would a manager who needs photos of the assembly floor for a presentation most likely do?
questions.zh: 需要廠區照片做簡報的主管，最可能會怎麼做？
options: Take pictures from inside the yellow lines
Contact the communications office
Ask the safety team member during the tour
Call extension 310

passages.title: Subject: Congratulations to Ms. Ramos
lines: To: All staff
From: Henry Walsh, President

I am pleased to announce that Ms. Maria Ramos has been promoted to Director of Operations. She will start in her new role on March 3, when she replaces Paul Chen, who is retiring after 22 years with the company.

Ms. Ramos joined us nine years ago as a junior buyer. Since then, she has worked in purchasing, at the factory, and most recently as manager of our Osaka branch. Under her leadership, the Osaka branch became the office with the highest profit in just three years, and its sales grew by 40 percent last year alone.

In her new role, Ms. Ramos will oversee our two factories and our delivery network. One of her first tasks will be to streamline the way orders move from our stores to the factories, which currently takes too long.
Ms. Ramos will move back to headquarters at the end of February. Until a new branch manager is chosen, Ken Mori, the assistant manager in Osaka, will lead the branch.

There will be a farewell party for Paul on Friday, February 28, at 6 p.m. in the main cafeteria. Please join us to thank Paul for his many years of hard work and to welcome Ms. Ramos to her new position.

questions.en: Why is Paul Chen leaving his position?
questions.zh: Paul Chen 為什麼要離開他的職位？
options: He was promoted to a new role.
He is moving to the Osaka branch.
He will run the delivery network.
He has decided to stop working.

questions.en: What is true about Ms. Ramos?
questions.zh: 關於 Ramos 女士，下列何者正確？
options: She has worked in more than one part of the company.
She joined the company 22 years ago.
She will lead the Osaka branch until a new manager is found.
She will plan the farewell party on February 28.

questions.en: What is suggested about the way orders currently move from the stores to the factories?
questions.zh: 關於目前訂單從門市送到工廠的流程，文中暗示了什麼？
options: It was designed by Paul Chen.
It needs to be made faster.
It works best at the Osaka branch.
It will be handled by Ken Mori.
